reader.requirement: At --std 85 a declarative section may begin USE [GLOBAL] BEFORE REPORTING identifier-1 (identifier-1 a report group, optionally qualified by its report-name); both the GLOBAL and the plain form must be accepted and run with the X.5.6.4 GR1 precedence (the declarative of the program that issued the GENERATE first, then a GLOBAL one of each containing program), and forms outside the format (missing BEFORE/REPORTING/identifier, GLOBAL misplaced, AFTER REPORTING, two operands, a non-group operand) must be refused. The single witness covers only USE Format 1.

refuter.evidence: At --std 85. GR1c three-level precedence the reader did not try: u5 outer USE GLOBAL, middle USE GLOBAL, GENERATE in outer/middle/inner -> 'OUTER N=001 / MIDDLE N=002 / MIDDLE N=003' (first qualifying, b); u6 middle declarative WITHOUT GLOBAL -> 'OUTER 001 / MIDDLE 002 / OUTER 003' (the non-GLOBAL middle one is skipped for the inner GENERATE, rule b then c). Class d other group types: u7 USE BEFORE REPORTING on a PAGE HEADING and a CONTROL FOOTING with SUM -> 'BEFORE PHG / BEFORE CFG S1=+0003 G=1 / BEFORE CFG S1=+0003 G=2', report HEAD/001/002/CF 0003/003/CF 0003 (sum counter is signed per the 1985 Sum Counter definition, so +0003 is right). Refusals of the XIII.4.9.3 SRs the format leans on: u1 same identifier-1 in two USE -> COBOL0897 (SR2 as amended); u3 GENERATE in the procedure -> COBOL2378 (SR3); u8 MOVE to control item G -> COBOL2378 (SR4); u4 USE not alone in its sentence -> COBOL0897 (SR1). cite.py: OK §1985:X.5.6.4 GR1; OK §1985:XIII.4.9.3 SR1, SR2, SR3, SR4.
